For any inputs, after calling Collect(...) on a correctly reentrancy-guarded C, MinSum remains unchanged (Collect cannot modify MinSum); removing the require in the guard allows a reentrant attacker to call SetMinSum during Collect and change MinSum, violating this rule for some inputs.

For all inputs, calling Collect(...) on the correct contract never changes MinSum (Collect cannot modify MinSum), while the mutant that removes the require in the nonReentrant_ modifier can be re-entered and allow a malicious receiver to call SetMinSum during Collect, changing MinSum.

For all inputs, calling Collect(...) on the correct contract never changes MinSum (Collect cannot cause MinSum to be modified), while the mutant that disables the nonReentrant_ require can be re-entered and let a malicious recipient call SetMinSum during Collect, changing MinSum.

For every input, calling Collect(...) on the correct contract C never changes MinSum (Collect cannot cause MinSum to be modified); the mutant that removes the require in the nonReentrant_ modifier can be re-entered by a malicious payable recipient which calls SetMinSum during Collect, causing MinSum to change for some inputs.
After a successful first call to SetMinSum, a second call to SetMinSum by the same caller does not revert (i.e. both calls succeed).
